From: rafael_mendes@redwood.ai
To: Alex Boyd <alex.boyd@aureliasys.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: camila_reyes@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-11T13:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Security intake: CAIQ + SIG scope and scheduling

Alex — appreciate the CAIQ. Quick prep notes before Tuesday’s call — call these our baseline so the meeting can focus on gaps and timelines: 

1) Logs & samples- We can provide request/response traces plus system-level inference logs. Preferred handoff: redwood will produce a redacted gzipped JSONL bundle (sample name: redwood-log-sample.tar.gz). We can host this on an S3 presigned link or push to your SFTP.
2) Evidence matrix- We’ll map CAIQ/SIG questions to artifacts (policy docs, diagrams, config screenshots). Typical turnaround for artifacts: 3–7 business days for standard items, 10–15 days for deeper engineering proofs (e.g., kernel-level telemetry).
3) KMS & encryption- We support customer-managed keys (CMK) in Dedicated and Private deployments; hosted API uses Redwood-managed KMS by default. We’ll surface the KMS architecture diagram on the call.
4) Data residency & backups- Primary data center is us-west-2. Dr/replication zones exist but are disabled by default for hosted customers; we’ll confirm for a given account if cross-region replication is enabled.

Action items for the call (we’ll propose owners live):
- Confirm exact CAIQ/SIG scope (Aurelia to confirm essential vs nice-to-have)
- Agree on log sample delivery method and retention window
- Identify any redlines for KMS or data residency

Looking forward — I’ll bring the evidence matrix template and a short checklist so we can assign owners during the call.

Rgds,
Rafael Mendes
Head of Security Integrations — Redwood Inference
[Attachment stub: redwood-log-sample.tar.gz]
